rows.question: For the RBAC action 'access_as_shared' (considering only IPv4 subnets), what are the average, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of subnet IP version with subtotals and a grand total, and—alongside those stats—what are the top 3 shared networks by subnet count, including each network ID, its subnet count, and the tenant ID of each subnet (with repeated network IDs suppressed)? Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH SubnetStats AS (
  SELECT
    s.id AS subnet_id,
    s.ip_version,
    s.tenant_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS subnet_count
  FROM subnets s
  JOIN ipallocations i ON s.id = i.subnet_id
  WHERE i.ip_address LIKE '%[0-9]%' AND s.ip_version = 4
  GROUP BY s.id, s.ip_version, s.tenant_id
),
TopNetworks AS (
  SELECT
    network_id,
    subnet_count
  FROM SubnetStats
  ORDER BY subnet_count DESC
  LIMIT 3
)
SELECT
  AVG(subnet_count) AS avg_subnet_count,
  STDDEV(subnet_count) AS variance,
  STDDEV(subnet_count) AS stddev,
  (
    SELECT
      network_id,
      subnet_count,
      tenant_id
    FROM SubnetStats
    WHERE network_id IN (
      SELECT
        network_id
      FROM SubnetStats
      ORDER BY subnet_count DESC
      LIMIT 3
    )
  ) AS top_3_networks
FROM SubnetStats
GROUP BY avg_subnet_count, variance, stddev

rows.question: For tenants that are in the top 10 by distinct DOWN ports and also in the top 10 by IPv4 subnet count, return the tenant ID, total distinct DOWN ports, whether any of those DOWN ports have an IP allocation, total IPv4 subnets, and whether any IPv4 subnet has a standard attribute record with a non-null updated-at timestamp—keeping only tenants where DOWN ports are more than 75% of their IPv4 subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  t.tenant_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.port_id) AS total_distinct_down_ports,
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT p.port_id) > 0 THEN 'Yes'
    ELSE 'No'
  END AS has_down_ports_with_ip_allocation,
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) AS total_ipv4_subnets,
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) > 0 THEN
      CASE
        WHEN EXISTS (
          SELECT
            1
          FROM
            subnets s
          JOIN
            standard_attr_id sai ON s.standard_attr_id = sai.id
          WHERE
            sai.updated_at IS NOT NULL
        ) THEN 'Yes'
        ELSE 'No'
      END
    ELSE 'No'
  END AS has_ipv4_subnet_with_updated_at
FROM
  ports p
JOIN
  subnets s ON p.network_id = s.id
JOIN
  ipallocations ia ON p.port_id = ia.port_id
JOIN
  ipamsubnets ips ON s.id = ips.id
JOIN
  tenant_id t ON s.tenant_id = t.id
WHERE
  p.status = 'DOWN'
GROUP BY
  t.tenant_id
HAVING
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.port_id) >= (
    SELECT
      COUNT(DISTINCT port_id)
    FROM
      ports
    WHERE
      status = 'DOWN'
  )
  AND COUNT(DISTINCT p.port_id) >= 0.75 * (
    SELECT
      COUNT(DISTINCT port_id)
    FROM
      ports
    WHERE
      status = 'DOWN'
  )
LIMIT 10

rows.question: How many distinct admin_state_up = 1 ports that are bound to a security group are there, and how many distinct DOWN ports belong to security groups whose number of DOWN ports is greater than the average number of DOWN ports per security group? Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH focused_whole_view AS (
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.id)
FROM ports AS p
WHERE
  p.admin_state_up = 1
)
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS distinct_up_ports,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p_down.id) AS distinct_down_ports
FROM ports AS p
INNER JOIN securitygrouprules AS gr ON p.id = gr.security_group_id
INNER JOIN securitygroups AS sg ON gr.security_group_id = sg.id
INNER JOIN ports AS p_down
  ON p_down.id = p_down.id
WHERE
  p.admin_state_up = 1
  AND p_down.admin_state_up = 0
  AND sg.id IN (
    SELECT
      sg.id
    FROM securitygroups AS sg
    JOIN (
      SELECT
        sg.id,
        COUNT(
          CASE
            WHEN p_down.admin_state_up = 0
            THEN p_down.id
            ELSE NULL
          END
        ) AS down_count
      FROM ports AS p_down
      JOIN securitygrouprules AS gr ON p_down.id = gr.security_group_id
      JOIN securitygroups AS sg ON gr.security_group_id = sg.id
      GROUP BY
        sg.id
    ) AS down_counts
    ON down_counts.down_count > (
      SELECT
        AVG(down_count)
        FROM (
          SELECT
            sg.id,
            COUNT(
              CASE
                WHEN p_down.admin_state_up = 0
                THEN p_down.id
                ELSE NULL
              END
            ) AS down_count
            FROM ports AS p_down
            JOIN securitygrouprules AS gr ON p_down.id = gr.security_group_id
            JOIN securitygroups AS sg ON gr.security_group_id = sg.id
            GROUP BY
              sg.id
          ) AS temp_down_counts
        )
)

rows.question: For external networks that are marked as default (IS_DEFAULT = 0), list each network’s ID, name, status, and ADMIN_STATE_UP, along with (1) the per-status average ADMIN_STATE_UP computed as a window over networks ordered by name, (2) the overall average of those per-status averages across all statuses, and (3) the overall benchmark ADMIN_STATE_UP across all such external networks and a category showing whether each network is ABOVE_BENCHMARK, BELOW_BENCHMARK, or AT_BENCHMARK versus that benchmark. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH external_default_networks AS (
  SELECT
    network_id,
    name,
    status,
    admin_state_up
  FROM externalnetworks
  WHERE
    is_default = 0
)
SELECT
  edn.network_id,
  edn.name,
  edn.status,
  edn.admin_state_up,
  AVG(edn.admin_state_up) OVER (PARTITION BY edn.name) AS per_network_avg_up,
  AVG(AVG(edn.admin_state_up) OVER (PARTITION BY edn.name)) AS overall_avg_up,
  CASE
    WHEN edn.admin_state_up >= AVG(AVG(edn.admin_state_up) OVER (PARTITION BY edn.name)) THEN 'ABOVE_BENCHMARK'
    WHEN edn.admin_state_up <= AVG(AVG(edn.admin_state_up) OVER (PARTITION BY edn.name)) THEN 'BELOW_BENCHMARK'
    ELSE 'AT_BENCHMARK'
  END AS benchmark_category
FROM external_default_networks AS edn

rows.question: For IPv4 subnets that are in the top 10 by DNS nameserver order range and that have DNS nameservers configured, return the subnet name, tenant ID, network ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, the allocation pool’s first and last IP (only where the first IP is the minimum for that subnet), the maximum subnet standard attribute ID over the current row and next 2 rows by subnet ID, plus the DNS nameserver order range and order variance. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
    s.subnet_name,
    s.tenant_id,
    s.network_id,
    s.ip_version,
    s.cidr,
    s.gateway_ip,
    s.enable_dhcp,
    (SELECT first_ip FROM ipamallocationpools WHERE ipam_subnet_id = s.id) AS allocation_pool_first_ip,
    (SELECT last_ip FROM ipamallocationpools WHERE ipam_subnet_id = s.id) AS allocation_pool_last_ip,
    (
        SELECT
            max(standard_attr_id)
        FROM
            subnets
        WHERE
            id IN (s.id, (SELECT id FROM subnets WHERE id = s.id LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1), (SELECT id FROM subnets WHERE id = s.id LIMIT 1 OFFSET 2))
    ) AS max_subnet_standard_attr_id,
    (SELECT order FROM dnsnameservers WHERE subnet_id = s.id) AS dns_nameserver_order,
    (
        SELECT
            order -
            (
                SELECT
                    order
                FROM
                    dnsnameservers
                WHERE
                    subnet_id = s.id
            )
        GROUP BY

    ) AS dns_nameserver_order_variance
FROM
    subnets s
JOIN
    dnsnameservers d ON s.id = d.subnet_id
WHERE
    s.id IN (
        SELECT
            id
        FROM
            subnets
        ORDER BY
            (SELECT order FROM dnsnameservers WHERE subnet_id = s.id) DESC
        LIMIT 10
    )
    AND s.id IN (SELECT id FROM dnsnameservers)
    AND s.enable_dhcp = 1
    AND s.ip_version = 4
    AND s.default_prefixlen = 24

rows.question: Show a combined report of DOWN ports that (1) lists ports by tenant with port ID, tenant ID (not repeated on consecutive rows), binding host, VIF type, allocated IP address, a row number ordered by IP address using a 2-preceding/1-following window, plus a subtotal row per tenant with the total number of DOWN ports; and (2) lists ports by VIF type with port name, MAC address, admin_state_up, binding host, the windowed average admin_state_up over 2 preceding and 2 following rows partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address, plus a subtotal row per VIF type with the total number of DOWN ports and the average of the windowed values, with VIF type not repeated on consecutive rows. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH ports_down AS (
  SELECT
    port_id,
    tenant_id,
    mac_address,
    admin_state_up,
    ip_address,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tenant_id ORDER BY ip_address ASC) AS row_num
  FROM ports
  WHERE
    admin_state_up = 0
),
tenant_down_ports AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS total_down_ports
  FROM ports_down
  GROUP BY
    tenant_id
),
vif_type_down_ports AS (
  SELECT
    vif_type,
    COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS total_down_ports,
    AVG(admin_state_up) OVER (PARTITION BY vif_type ORDER BY ip_address ASC ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) AS avg_admin_state_up
  FROM ports_down
),
final_result AS (
  SELECT
    p.port_id,
    p.tenant_id,
    p.mac_address,
    p.admin_state_up,
    CASE
      WHEN p.row_num = 1 THEN 'First'
      WHEN p.row_num = 2 THEN 'Second'
      WHEN p.row_num = 3 THEN 'Third'
      ELSE ''
    END AS rank_ip,
    CASE
      WHEN v.avg_admin_state_up IS NULL THEN NULL
      ELSE v.avg_admin_state_up
    END AS avg_admin_state_up,
    td.total_down_ports,
    td.total_down_ports_per_vif_type
  FROM ports_down AS p
  JOIN tenant_down_ports AS td
    ON p.tenant_id = td.tenant_id
  LEFT JOIN vif_type_down_ports AS v ON p.vif_type = v.vif_type
)
SELECT
  *
FROM final_result
ORDER BY
  rank_ip,
  mac_address

rows.question: For ACTIVE networks, list each network’s name, status, and admin_state_up together with its RBAC action and target tenant (including the distinct RBAC target-tenant count per network and the dense-rank window column), and also include—alongside every such network/RBAC row—the per-(port status, device owner) port counts for ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', the earliest standard-attribute updated timestamp for each group, and each group’s deviation from the overall average port count. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH ports_active AS (
  SELECT
    p.id AS port_id,
    p.name AS port_name,
    p.device_owner AS port_device_owner,
    p.status AS port_status
  FROM ports AS p
  WHERE
    p.admin_state_up = 1
),
network_port_counts AS (
  SELECT
    n.id AS network_id,
    n.name AS network_name,
    n.status AS network_status,
    n.admin_state_up,
    COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS port_count
  FROM networks AS n
  JOIN ports AS p
    ON n.id = p.network_id
  GROUP BY
    n.id,
    n.name,
    n.status,
    n.admin_state_up
),
port_timestamps AS (
  SELECT
    p.id AS port_id,
    MIN(sa.updated_at) AS earliest_updated_at
  FROM ports AS p
  JOIN standard_attributes AS sa
    ON p.standard_attr_id = sa.id
  GROUP BY
    p.id
)
SELECT
  n.network_name,
  n.network_status,
  n.admin_state_up,
  pc.port_count,
  pt.earliest_updated_at,
  (
    pc.port_count - (
      SELECT
        AVG(port_count)
        FROM (
          SELECT
            pc.port_count AS port_count
            FROM network_port_counts AS pc
          ) AS avg_counts
    )
  ) AS port_count_variance
FROM network_port_counts AS pc
JOIN networks AS n
  ON pc.port_count = n.id
JOIN ports_active AS pa
  ON pc.port_count = pa.port_id
JOIN port_timestamps AS pt
  ON pa.port_id = pt.port_id
ORDER BY
  n.network_name

rows.question: For ports whose status is DOWN and that also have a standard attribute ID above the average for their resource type, list each port’s port ID and tenant ID along with host, VIF type, allocated IP address, the IP-address-ordered row number (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), the tenant’s total number of DOWN ports, the overall average DOWN-port count benchmark and the tenant usage category (HIGH_USER/LOW_USER/AVERAGE_USER), plus the port’s MAC address and the running sum of standard attribute IDs within its resource type. Do not return any rounded answers. Classify the tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
  ports_down AS (
    SELECT
      p.port_id,
      p.tenant_id,
      p.host,
      p.VIF_Type,
      ip.Allocated_IP,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ip.Allocated_IP) AS IP_address_ordered_row_number,
      COUNT(p.port_id) OVER (PARTITION BY p.tenant_id) AS tenant_total_down_ports,
      (SELECT AVG(standard_attr_id) FROM standardattributes) AS overall_average_down_port_count,
      CASE
        WHEN (SELECT COUNT(p.port_id) FROM ports p WHERE p.tenant_id = p.tenant_id AND p.status = 'DOWN') > ((SELECT AVG(standard_attr_id) FROM standardattributes) * 2) THEN 'HIGH_USER'
        WHEN (SELECT COUNT(p.port_id) FROM ports p WHERE p.tenant_id = p.tenant_id AND p.status = 'DOWN') < ((SELECT AVG(standard_attr_id) FROM standardattributes) * 0.5) THEN 'LOW_USER'
        ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER'
      END AS tenant_usage_category,
      p.mac_address,
      SUM(standard_attr_id) OVER (PARTITION BY p.resource_type) AS running_sum_standard_attr_id
    FROM ports p
    JOIN ipallocations ip ON p.port_id = ip.port_id
    CROSS JOIN (SELECT AVG(standard_attr_id) FROM standardattributes) AS avg_attr
    WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'
  )
SELECT
  port_id,
  tenant_id,
  host,
  VIF_Type,
  Allocated_IP,
  IP_address_ordered_row_number,
  tenant_total_down_ports,
  overall_average_down_port_count,
  tenant_usage_category,
  mac_address,
  running_sum_standard_attr_id
FROM ports_down

rows.question: How many DOWN ports have IP allocations (from the DOWN-port per-network allocation analysis) and how many administratively up ports have port security bindings (from the admin-up port security benchmark analysis)? Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each port as 'HIGH_SECURITY' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_SECURITY' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_SECURITY'.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH port_security_levels AS (
    SELECT
        p.id AS port_id,
        CASE
            WHEN psb.port_security_enabled = 1 THEN 1.0
            ELSE 0.0
        END AS security_level
    FROM ports AS p
    JOIN ipallocations AS ia ON p.id = ia.port_id
    JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id
    WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1
)
SELECT
    COUNT(CASE WHEN security_level >= 0.5 THEN port_id END) AS high_security,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN security_level <= -0.5 THEN port_id END) AS low_security,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN security_level BETWEEN -0.5 AND 0.5 THEN port_id END) AS average_security
FROM port_security_levels

rows.question: For ports whose status is DOWN, show each port’s ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also include, per host, the total number of DOWN-port IP allocations and each row’s deviation from the average DOWN-port IP allocations per host, and attach the DOWN-status port-security-binding rollup statistics (admin-state label plus the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of port security bindings per port, including subtotal/grand-total style labels). Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH down_ports AS (
    SELECT
        p.id AS port_id,
        p.tenant_id,
        dp.host,
        CASE
            WHEN p.protocol = 'HTTP' THEN 'HTTP'
            WHEN p.protocol = 'HTTPS' THEN 'HTTPS'
            ELSE 'TCP'
        END AS vif_type,
        ip.ip_address,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ip.ip_address ORDER BY ip.ip_address ASC ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) AS row_num
    FROM ports AS p
    JOIN ipallocations AS ip ON p.id = ip.port_id
    JOIN down_ports dp ON p.id = dp.port_id
    WHERE dp.port_status = 'DOWN'
),
port_security_rollup AS (
    SELECT
        port_id,
        admin_state_up,
        VARIANCE(port_security_enabled) AS variance,
        STDDEV(port_security_enabled) AS stddev
    FROM portsecuritybindings
    GROUP BY port_id
)
SELECT
    dp.port_id,
    dp.tenant_id,
    dp.host,
    dp.vif_type,
    dp.ip_address,
    dp.row_num,
    psr.variance,
    psr.stddev,
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) FROM ipallocations WHERE port_id = dp.port_id AND port_status = 'DOWN') AS down_ip_count,
    (dp.variance - psr.variance) AS ip_variance,
    psr.stddev
FROM down_ports dp
JOIN port_security_rollup psr ON dp.port_id = psr.port_id
ORDER BY dp.ip_address

rows.question: For each of the top 10 tenants with the highest total number of IP allocations on administratively up ports (with at least one IP allocation), list the tenant ID, the total number of such ports, the total number of IP allocations across those ports, whether the tenant has any floating IPs allocated, and the average (across that tenant’s ports) deviation of each port’s IP allocation count from the global average IP allocation count across all such ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  t.tenant_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT po.id) AS total_ports,
  SUM(ip_alloc.ip_address) AS total_allocations,
  SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (
    SELECT
      1
    FROM
      ipallocations i
    JOIN
      ports po ON i.subnet_id = po.network_id
    WHERE
      po.tenant_id = t.tenant_id AND po.admin_state_up = 1
    ) THEN 1 ELSE 0
  ) AS has_floating_ips,
  AVG(
    (
      COUNT(DISTINCT ip_alloc.ip_address) -
      (
        SELECT
          AVG(COUNT(DISTINCT ip_alloc.ip_address))
        FROM
          ipallocations ip_alloc
        JOIN
          ports po ON ip_alloc.subnet_id = po.network_id
        WHERE
          po.tenant_id = t.tenant_id AND po.admin_state_up = 1
      )
    )
  ) AS avg_allocation_deviation
FROM
  ipallocations ip_alloc
JOIN
  ports po ON ip_alloc.subnet_id = po.network_id
JOIN
  vpnservices vs ON po.tenant_id = vs.tenant_id
JOIN
  ipamsubnets is ON ip_alloc.ip_address = is.id
JOIN
  networks n ON is.neutron_subnet_id = n.id
JOIN
  ipamallocations am ON is.id = am.ip_address
JOIN
  subnets s ON is.id = s.id
JOIN
  tenants t ON po.tenant_id = t.id
WHERE
  po.admin_state_up = 1
GROUP BY
  t.tenant_id
ORDER BY
  t.tenant_id
LIMIT 10

Also include the tenant’s total number of DOWN ports and the average DOWN-port count across all tenants, plus the port’s MAC address, the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within its security group (ordered by standard attribute ID), the security group’s total number of DOWN ports, and that security group’s deviation from the average DOWN-port count across all security groups.   p.mac_address,
  p.name AS port_name,

  pt.current_dns_name,

rows.question: For the top 10 tenants with the highest total number of IP allocations on administratively up ports (with at least one IP allocation), and where more than 75% of the tenant’s ports are in DOWN status, return the tenant ID, total number of such administratively up ports, total IP allocations across them, whether the tenant has any floating IPs, plus the number of DOWN ports whose standard attribute ID is above the DOWN-port average for their resource type and the average running sum of standard attribute IDs for those qualifying DOWN ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH focused_whole_view AS (
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.id)
FROM ports AS p
WHERE
  p.admin_state_up = 1
)
SELECT
    tenant_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS total_up_ports,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ip.port_id) AS total_ip_allocations,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ports p JOIN ipallocations ip ON p.id = ip.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND p.status = 'UP') THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS has_floating_ips,
    AVG(s.id) AS avg_standard_attribute_id,
    SUM(s.id) AS running_sum_standard_attribute_id
FROM
    ports p
JOIN
    ipallocations ip ON p.id = ip.port_id
JOIN

rows.question: For ports whose status is DOWN, restricted to tenants that are in the top 10 by total IP allocations on administratively up ports (with at least one IP allocation), list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). WITH PortStats AS (
    SELECT
        p.port_id,

),

    SELECT
        tenant_id,

rows.question: For the top 10 tenants ranked by the highest coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) (standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) divided by average) of allocated IP address string lengths for ports with port security enabled, list each tenant’s ID, their coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP), and whether they have any ACTIVE, DOWN, or BUILD ports; and for those same tenants, show details of their DOWN ports including port ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), the tenant’s total number of DOWN ports, the average DOWN-port count across tenants as a benchmark, and the tenant’s DOWN-port usage category (HIGH_USER/LOW_USER/AVERAGE_USER). Do not return any rounded answers. Classify the tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH tenant_ip_variation AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    AVG(LENGTH(ip_address)) AS avg_ip_length,
    STDDEV(LENGTH(ip_address)) AS stddev_ip_length
  FROM ipallocations
  WHERE port_security_enabled = 1
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
down_port_details AS (
  SELECT
    pp.port_id,
    p.host,
    ia.ip_address,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ia.ip_address ASC, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ia.ip_address ASC) - 2) AS port_rank,
    p.tenant_id
  FROM portbindingports pp
  JOIN ports p ON pp.port_id = p.id
  JOIN ipallocations ia ON pp.port_id = ia.port_id
  WHERE p.admin_state_up = 0
),
down_port_category AS (
  SELECT
    tenant_id,
    AVG(LENGTH(ip_address)) AS avg_ip_length,
    SUM(CASE WHEN LENGTH(ip_address) > 16 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_user_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN LENGTH(ip_address) < 8 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS low_user_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN LENGTH(ip_address) BETWEEN 8 AND 16 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS average_user_count
  FROM (
    SELECT
      tenant_id,
      LENGTH(ip_address) AS ip_address_length
    FROM down_port_details
  ) AS temp
  GROUP BY tenant_id
),
tenant_summary AS (
    SELECT
        tenant_id,
        avg_ip_length,
        stddev_ip_length
    FROM tenant_ip_variation
),
final_result AS (
    SELECT
        t.tenant_id,
        t.avg_ip_length,
        (t.avg_ip_length / t.stddev_ip_length) AS coefficient_of_variation,
        CASE
            WHEN t.avg_ip_length > (t.avg_ip_length * 1.5) THEN 'HIGH_USER'
            WHEN t.avg_ip_length < (t.avg_ip_length * 0.5) THEN 'LOW_USER'
            ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER'
        END AS down_port_usage,
        d.port_id,
        d.host,
        d.ip_address,
        d.port_rank,
        d.tenant_id,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY d.tenant_id) AS total_down_ports,
        (SELECT AVG(avg_ip_length) FROM tenant_ip_variation) AS average_down_port_count,
        (SELECT down_port_usage FROM down_port_category WHERE tenant_id = d.tenant_id) AS down_port_usage
    FROM tenant_ip_variation t
    JOIN down_port_details d ON t.tenant_id = d.tenant_id
    JOIN down_port_category dpc ON dpc.tenant_id = dpc.tenant_id
)
SELECT *
FROM final_result
ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC
LIMIT 10

rows.question: For subnets on networks that have a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', show each subnet name and gateway IP (including subtotals per subnet name and a grand total) along with the maximum IP version (keeping only rows where this maximum is greater than 3). Also, for any matching IPv4 subnet name, include its dense rank of the associated standard attribute ID ordered by the standard attribute updated-at timestamp (using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows), the overall average of these dense ranks as a benchmark, and the subnet’s rank category (HIGH_RANK/LOW_RANK/AVERAGE_RANK). Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each subnet as 'HIGH_RANK' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_RANK' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_RANK'.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH subnet_network_data AS (
    SELECT
        s.name AS subnet_name,
        s.gateway_ip,
        s.ip_version AS subnet_ip_version,
        n.status AS network_status,
        n.admin_state_up AS network_admin_state_up,
        n.availability_zone_hints AS network_availability_zone_hints
    FROM
        subnets s
    JOIN
        networks n ON s.network_id = n.id
),
standard_attribute_data AS (
    SELECT
        sa.id AS standard_attr_id,
        sa.updated_at AS standard_attr_updated_at
    FROM
        standardattributes sa
),
ranked_standard_attributes AS (
    SELECT
        sa.standard_attr_id,
        sa.updated_at AS standard_attr_updated_at,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY sa.updated_at DESC, sa.standard_attr_id) AS row_num
    FROM
        standard_attribute_data sa
),
subnet_rankings AS (
    SELECT
        sr.standard_attr_id,
        sr.standard_attr_updated_at,
        sr.row_num,
        CASE
            WHEN sr.row_num * 1.0 <= (SELECT AVG(row_num) FROM ranked_standard_attributes) * 0.5 THEN 'HIGH_RANK'
            WHEN sr.row_num * 1.0 > (SELECT AVG(row_num) FROM ranked_standard_attributes) * 0.5 AND sr.row_num * 1.0 <= (SELECT AVG(row_num) FROM ranked_standard_attributes) * 0.8 THEN 'LOW_RANK'
            ELSE 'AVERAGE_RANK'
        END AS rank_category
    FROM
        ranked_standard_attributes sr
)
SELECT
    sd.subnet_name,
    sd.gateway_ip,
    MAX(sd.ip_version) AS max_ip_version,
    sd.rank_category
FROM
    subnet_network_data sd
JOIN
    subnet_rankings sd_rank ON sd.subnet_name = sd_rank.subnet_name
GROUP BY
    sd.subnet_name, sd.gateway_ip, sd.rank_category
ORDER BY
    sd.subnet_name

rows.question: For IPv4 subnets whose network RBAC action is set to 'access_as_shared', what are the subnet name, CIDR, RBAC target tenant, the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within the IP version (ordered by standard attribute ID), the total number of such shared subnets per target tenant and the average of those totals across all target tenants, along with the subnet’s standard attribute resource type and the dense rank of its standard attribute (ordered by the standard attribute updated-at timestamp using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows)? Do not return any rounded answers.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH SubnetsWithSharedAccess AS (
  SELECT
    id,
    tenant_id,
    cidr,
    ip_version,
    rbac_action,
    standard_attr_id,
    standard_attr_id_updated_at
  FROM subnets
  WHERE
    ip_version = 4
    AND rbac_action = 'access_as_shared'
)
SELECT
  SUBSTRING(s.name, 1, 30) AS "Subnet Name",
  s.cidr AS "CIDR",
  s.tenant_id AS "RBAC Target Tenant",
  SUM(s.standard_attr_id) OVER (PARTITION BY s.cidr) AS "Running Sum of Subnet Standard Attribute IDs",
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.tenant_id) AS "Total Number of Shared Subnets per Target Tenant",
  AVG(COUNT(DISTINCT s.tenant_id)) OVER () AS "Average of Total Subnet Counts Across All Target Tenants",
  s.ip_version AS "Subnet Standard Attribute Resource Type",
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY s.standard_attr_id_updated_at ASC,
    (
      SELECT
        standard_attr_id_updated_at
      FROM SubnetsWithSharedAccess
      ORDER BY
        standard_attr_id_updated_at ASC
      LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1
    ) ASC,
    (
      SELECT
        standard_attr_id_updated_at
      FROM SubnetsWithSharedAccess
      ORDER BY
        standard_attr_id_updated_at ASC
      LIMIT 2 OFFSET 1
    ) ASC
  ) AS "Dense Rank of Standard Attribute"
FROM subnets s
JOIN SubnetsWithSharedAccess swsh ON s.id = swsh.id
GROUP BY s.id, s.tenant_id, s.cidr, s.ip_version
ORDER BY s.standard_attr_id_updated_at ASC
